chains.title: Risk allele A weakens an AP-2 (TFAP2A) site in the distal IRF6 enhancer, lowering IRF6 in oral epithelium/periderm
chains.element: Distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2863563 (Ensembl enhancer ENSR1_B3JM9C) ~10 kb upstream of IRF6
chains.cell_type: Oral epithelium/periderm of the developing lip (asserted from literature, not from data in this case)

links.claim: TFAP2A has its own QBiC-SELEX model that passes the gate at this variant with effect +2.176 (z 11.94, rank 41/997; ref 96.3th vs alt 100.0th percentile k-mer strength), so the alt G allele binds AP-2 more and the cleft risk allele A binds less; the whole AP-2 group agrees in direction (TFAP2B z 23.98, TFAP2C, TFAP2E). TFAP2A is chosen within the group from its known craniofacial-ectoderm role, not from data here; no ENCODE ChIP peak supports occupancy, though no relevant biosample may have been assayed
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 5.3, H3K27ac z 5.0, maxima across biosamples) and is annotated as a regulatory_region_variant in an Ensembl enhancer

IRF6 is 9.7 kb from the element and is a leading L2G gene (up to 0.67; 0.16 in the orofacial cleft set), and the variant is a significant IRF6 eQTL in GTEx brain (NES -0.62); but UTP25/DIEXF has the highest L2G (0.75) and more eQTL tissues, so the IRF6 assignment is not settled, and the brain eQTL direction (alt G lowers IRF6) runs opposite to the AP-2 gain-of-binding prediction

No expression context was supplied and no craniofacial epigenome data are cited; the oral epithelium/periderm assignment rests only on prior IRF6 cleft literature, which concerns other SNPs at the locus

The A allele is the orofacial cleft risk allele (p 2e-06, PIP 0.05), and literature states that functional SNPs near IRF6 account for most of the cleft risk at this locus, although rs642961 is not named in the quoted text; a tissue-specific drop in enhancer output is the proposed, not demonstrated, mechanism

grades_v0.reason: The AP-2 group (E13) is a QBiC-SELEX prediction only, alt G binds more, which matches the claim that A binds less. TFAP2A was chosen from the group because of its craniofacial role, not from any data in this case. TFAP2A has the weakest model (z 11.94), and the text calls it 'same direction' without a cited per-model effect.

E03 places the variant in a dELS cCRE with DNase z 5.3 and H3K27ac z 5.0, and E01 gives an Ensembl enhancer annotation. These are maxima over biosamples, so they are not tissue-specific. The claim that this is an MCS9.7-like enhancer is not shown by the cited evidence.

IRF6 is 9.7 kb away and has L2G up to 0.67 (E05), but UTP25 has the best L2G (0.75) and shares the same TSS neighbourhood. The claim that IRF6 is the top-scoring gene is therefore overstated. Four TRAF3IP3 eQTL credible sets exist. No perturbation or enhancer-gene link is cited.
No expression context or epithelial data was provided. E06a and E06c are IRF6 locus and promoter-SNP literature and say nothing about periderm or oral epithelium at this variant.

E04 shows the A allele associated with orofacial clefts (p 2e-06), and E06a says two functional SNPs near IRF6 account for most of the risk. E06a does not name rs642961, and the PIP for clefts is only 0.05. Nothing cited shows that reduced IRF6 enhancer activity is the mechanism for this SNP. 'Accepted mechanism' is over-claimed.

G003 (E08) shows a strong alt-binds-more signal, and SPDEF (E09) agrees in direction. ELF3 is chosen by an expectation about epithelial expression with no expression data. No ELF3 model result is shown, and the group has 25+ TFs. The best model is ETV5, and ELF3 coverage is asserted without a lookup.
E03 and E01 show a dELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac, as described, though these are maxima across biosamples.
IRF6 is the nearest gene and has L2G 0.16 for the orofacial clefts set (E05). UTP25 scores higher overall, and no variant-to-gene perturbation or eQTL is cited.
E06a is only a statement about IRF6 locus SNPs and does not mention ELF3, SPDEF or epithelial expression. No expression data were provided.
E04 gives the A allele association with clefts. The claim that loss of an activating ETS input lowers IRF6 is speculation, with no perturbation evidence.

The TEA group (E10) is strong with alt binding less, so ref A binds more, which is consistent with the claim. It is a prediction only. TEAD1 is chosen as the strongest model, with no data on which paralogue is expressed.
E03 and E01 show an active dELS cCRE overlapping the variant, though the values are maxima over biosamples.
IRF6 is the nearest gene with moderate L2G, but UTP25 scores higher (0.75) and no enhancer-gene link is shown.
No evidence IDs are cited, and the claim of TEAD/YAP activity in craniofacial epithelium rests on prior knowledge alone.

E04 only shows the association. The chain admits the direction of the effect is not established, and a repressive TEAD role on the risk allele is speculative. Predicted direction is internally ambiguous.
G005 (E16) shows ref A binding more, but members disagree on direction. SOX2 is chosen as the strongest model without data on which SOX factor is relevant.
E03 supports a dELS cCRE containing the variant, though the values are maxima over biosamples.
IRF6 is nearest but is not the best-linked gene, since UTP25 has the highest L2G. Calling it 'nearest and best-linked' is over-claimed.
No evidence is cited and no expression data are available.
E04 gives only the association. No direction of effect on IRF6 is stated or supported for a SOX input.

grades_final.reason: E18 shows a QBiC-SELEX TFAP2A own-model gate pass (+2.176, alt binds more) and the AP-2 group agrees in direction, but this is a binding prediction alone. E19 shows no ChIP peak at the variant. TFAP2A was picked from known biology, not from data.

E01 and E03 place the variant in the dELS cCRE EH38E2863563 with high DNase (z 5.3) and H3K27ac (z 5.0) and in an Ensembl enhancer. These are maxima over biosamples, but the epigenomic context directly supports an element.

IRF6 is 9.7 kb away, has L2G up to 0.67 and has a GTEx brain eQTL, but UTP25 scores higher. There is no perturbation or enhancer-gene link. The IRF6 eQTL is only in cerebellum, and alt G lowers IRF6 there, which conflicts with the chain's own title claim of a lower-IRF6 mechanism through A weakening binding.
E06a cites no oral epithelium or periderm data and concerns other SNPs. No expression or chromatin evidence for the claimed cell type was given.

E04 shows an A-allele orofacial cleft association (p 2e-06), and E06a says functional SNPs near IRF6 drive risk but does not name rs642961. The PIP is only 0.05. The mechanistic link from enhancer output to cleft is not demonstrated, and the quote may point to other SNPs.

The Ets groups (E08, E09) show strong alt-binding-more predictions, but this is binding prediction only. ELF3's own z and effect were not retrieved, so no ELF3 lookup supports it. ELF3 was chosen without a data-based reason, and the SPDEF/ETV5 signal does not stand in for ELF3. A qbic_tf_detail lookup for ELF3 is needed to confirm its own_model status and direction.
E03 and E01 show a dELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac overlapping the variant, directly supporting an enhancer element.
IRF6 is the nearest gene with L2G 0.16 in the cleft set, but UTP25 is higher and no eQTL or perturbation evidence is cited for IRF6. The proximity and L2G are indirect.
No evidence IDs are cited, and the chain itself states the epithelial assignment is unsupported.
E04 supports only the A-allele cleft association. The claim that ETS loss on A lowers IRF6 and raises risk is conditional, and no evidence supports the direction.

E10 shows a TEAD group with own models where alt binds less (z -40.19), so ref A binds more, and the direction is consistent. This is a binding prediction only, with no occupancy data. TEAD1 was picked among paralogues without a reason.
E03 and E01 show an active dELS cCRE (DNase z 5.3, H3K27ac z 5.0) containing the variant.
IRF6 proximity (9.7 kb) and moderate L2G are only indirect, UTP25 scores higher, and no eQTL or perturbation evidence is cited for IRF6.
No evidence IDs are cited and nothing bears on TEAD/YAP activity or craniofacial tissue.
E04 supports only the A-allele cleft association. The effect direction of TEAD binding on IRF6 is explicitly unestablished, so the chain's direction is incomplete.

E18 and E13 give the same TFAP2A prediction as H1, which is a binding prediction alone with no ChIP support (E19 shows none and is not cited here). The claim that AP-2 acts as a repressor is not evidenced.
E03 and E01 show the dELS cCRE overlapping the variant with nearby genes including UTP25 and C1orf74. This supports an element, and the 12.0 kb distance from the UTP25 TSS is given in E02.

UTP25 has the best L2G (0.75, E05). GTEx (E20) shows DIEXF eQTLs in many tissues (e.g. fibroblasts NES -0.23, p 1.9e-14) and TRAF3IP3 in blood, which is genetic colocalization-type evidence. The direction (alt G lowers DIEXF) is consistent across most tissues, though brain shows the opposite sign. The AP-2 repressor explanation is speculative, but the gene link itself is supported. Note that UTP25 and DIEXF are asserted to be the same gene without a cited mapping.
E20 shows eQTLs in fibroblasts, artery, blood and adipose, which gives some context for those cells. The chain itself concedes that the cleft-relevant cell type is not identified.

E04 and E05 show the strongest GWAS signals are blood pressure (p 6e-12, effect allele G), so the vascular link is plausible genetically. But E05 PIPs are low (0.05-0.10), and cleft association is explained away by an unsupported secondary or linked-variant claim, so the connection to the cleft phenotype is not shown.
